issues.legal_issue: Tenant-protection provisions covering earlier tenancies apply to an appeal in an ejectment suit that remains pending when the provisions take effect.
material_facts: The landlords sued to evict their tenants after the leases expired, and trial courts decreed eviction before the tenant-protection law took effect.
The tenants appealed, and those appeals were pending when the law took effect.
The leases permitted the tenants to build residential houses, and the appellate courts found that permanent houses had been built within five years of the leases.
The law extended its protection to tenancies created before it took effect and protected qualifying tenants from eviction except for non-payment of rent.
issues.conclusion: The tenant-protection provisions applied to the pending appeals, which were continuations of the suits; the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A statutory provision operates retrospectively when express terms provide for it or when that intention clearly follows from its words and context. Although legislation affecting vested rights is ordinarily construed prospectively absent such an indication, the Act’s provision applying to tenancies created before its commencement and section 5(1)(a)’s protection of tenants who had already built qualifying structures showed an intention to apply retrospectively. Because an appeal is a continuation of the suit, section 5(1)(a) applied to an appeal pending when the Act took effect. The Court referred to Re Athlumney, Ex parte Wilson, (1898) 2 Q.B.D. 547.

predicates.tenant_protective_law_covers_prior_tenan: The law extends its tenant protections to tenancies created before the law took effect.
predicates.qualifying_structure_built: The tenant built a permanent residential or business structure within the required period under a contractual right or with the landlord’s knowledge and acquiescence.
predicates.ejectment_appeal_pending_at_commencement: An appeal from an ejectment decision remained pending when the tenant-protection law took effect.

issues.definition: When a tenant-protective law covers earlier tenancies, a tenant has built a qualifying structure, and an ejectment appeal is pending when the law takes effect, the appeal is governed by the tenant protection.
